summary: An all-steel lookout, 24.4 m (80 ft) high, was reported completed about a quarter mile east of Badger, Manitoba, in August 1947.

events.note: Carillon News report of August 22, 1947, quoted on Canada's Fire Lookouts, says the tower was completed about a quarter mile east of Badger.

evidence.supports: Tower completed about 1/4 mile east of Badger
evidence.quote: The new fire look-out tower has been completed about 1/4 mile east of Badger.
It is of all steel construction and is 80 ft. high.

evidence.supports: Badger is in the Rural Municipality of Piney
evidence.quote: The building was moved to Badger in the Rural Municipality of Piney where it is used as a private cottage.

evidence.supports: Most Manitoba fire lookout towers have been removed
evidence.quote: Fire lookout towers were once commonly used to watch for forest fires in Manitoba but most of them have been removed.

sources.title: Canadian National Railway Station (Badger, RM of Piney)
Woodridge Fire Tower (Woodridge, Woodridge Provincial Park)

notes_for_editor: Single source for the tower: the 1947 Carillon News item as quoted on Canada's Fire Lookouts. The newspaper original was not checked, and no other source describing this tower turned up in two searches. The record has no local_unit; the Manitoba Historical Society places Badger in the Rural Municipality of Piney, so the editor may want to add it (not a correction). The record's coordinates (49.18699, -95.95187) are not checked against any source. Lead, not cited: a search summary mentioned Pine Valley Echoes: A History of Badger, Menisino and Piney (1988), a local history that may say whether a lookout stood near Badger; it was not read. Not related: the 1947 Rainbow Tower carillon in Niagara Falls, Ontario, and the Badger lookouts in the United States.
